title: At the Bank
objectives: I can name money, accounts and bank cards in German
I can say that I go to the bank and that I am at the bank
I can use the most important bank verbs, also in the Perfekt
I can name the details of my account (Kontonummer, IBAN, Kontostand)

vocab.note: die Bank = bank; die Bank (pl. Bänke) = bench

expressions.en: I am going to the bank.

expressions.de: Guten Tag, ich möchte 100 Euro auf mein Konto einzahlen.
expressions.en: Good day, I would like to pay 100 euros into my account.

expressions.de: Ich muss heute etwas Geld abheben.
expressions.en: I have to withdraw some money today.

expressions.de: Wo kann man hier Dollar in Euro wechseln?
expressions.en: Where can one change dollars into euros here?

grammar.title: Wohin? zur Bank – Wo? in der Bank
grammar.body: **Wohin?** (where to) → **zur Bank gehen**. **Wo?** (where) → **in der Bank sein**. *zur* = *zu* + *der*. In southern Germany people also say **auf der Bank sein**. Do not confuse *die Bank* (money) with *die Bank* (bench, plural *die Bänke*).

examples.de: Wohin gehst du? – Ich gehe zur Bank.
examples.en: Where are you going? – I am going to the bank.

examples.de: Wo bist du? – Ich bin in der Bank.
examples.en: Where are you? – I am at the bank.

grammar.title: Money verbs and their Perfekt
grammar.body: The verbs below form the Perfekt with **haben**. Separable verbs put **-ge-** between the prefix and the stem (*einzahlen – eingezahlt*). Verbs with the inseparable prefix **über-** or **er-** have no *ge-* (*überweisen – überwiesen*, *eröffnen – eröffnet*).

examples.de: Er möchte sein Geld in ein Haus anlegen.
examples.en: He wants to invest his money in a house.

examples.de: Wenn man neu in Deutschland ist, soll man ein Konto eröffnen.
examples.en: When you are new in Germany, you should open an account.

examples.de: Ich ziehe um. Ich möchte mein Konto schließen.
examples.en: I am moving. I would like to close my account.

grammar.title: Two common accounts
grammar.body: In Germany the most common account is the **Girokonto** (current account): your salary comes in and you can pay and make transfers from it. From a **Sparkonto** (savings account, also *Tagesgeldkonto*) you cannot make such transactions. The plural of *das Konto* is **die Konten** or **die Kontos**.

grammar.title: Details for transfers
grammar.body: For an online transfer (**eine Überweisung**) you need the recipient's **IBAN**. For all banks in Germany the IBAN starts with **DE**. For international payments you also need the **BIC**; for payments within Germany the **Bankleitzahl** can be used. The account holder is **der Kontoinhaber**; the **Kontonummer** (up to ten digits) is given when you open an account.

grammar.title: Bank statement, cards and PIN
grammar.body: The **Kontoauszug** shows the **Kontostand** (or **Saldo**), the **Einnahmen** and the **Ausgaben**. You can withdraw money at the bank or at the **Geldautomat** (in Austria and Switzerland: **Bankomat**). In Germany people mostly use the **EC-Karte** or **Girokarte**; there is also the **Kreditkarte**. Every card has a **PIN** (**Geheimzahl**). If you lose a card you must have it blocked (**die Karte sperren lassen**).

mistakes.why: Going to an institution is usually *zur Bank*.
Separable verb: *ge* goes between prefix and stem; only one *ge*.

pronunciation.tip: Round your lips for 'oo' and say 'ee': *Überweisung, Münze, Kontoauszüge*.
At the beginning of a word 'sp' sounds like 'shp': *sparen, Sparkasse, Sparkonto*.

lines.de: Guten Tag, ich möchte 100 Euro auf mein Konto einzahlen.
lines.en: Good day, I would like to pay 100 euros into my account.

lines.de: Haben Sie ein Sparkonto oder ein Girokonto?
lines.en: Do you have a savings account or a current account?

lines.de: Hier ist meine EC-Karte. Die Nummer steht auf der Karte.
lines.en: Here is my debit card. The number is on the card.

tip: Many people in Germany pay by card, but it is still wise to carry some cash (Bargeld) with you.

exercises.instructions: Match the German words with their English meanings.

summary: Wohin? zur Bank gehen. Wo? in der Bank sein.
Money words: das Geld, der Geldschein, die Münze, das Kleingeld, das Bargeld.
Verbs: einzahlen, abheben, anlegen, sparen, wechseln, überweisen, eröffnen, schließen.
Accounts: das Girokonto (everyday) and das Sparkonto (savings). IBAN starts with DE.
Cards: die EC-Karte, die Kreditkarte; every card has a PIN (Geheimzahl).
